pr_title: Fix focus returning to the lounge search textbox while password is being checked
pr_body:
Closes #14779 again.

I added new (more isolated tests) then found the previous tests I wrote eventually. Let me know if you'd prefer one of the two were removed. They are both testing slightly different scenarios right now.

I did also consider setting the textbox to disabled while the password submission process is happening, but probably not required.
pr_comments:
> Let me know if you'd prefer one of the two were removed

I'd be fine with both staying despite the scope overlap, the multiplayer screen one is also checking navigation flow. Although if I were to choose one I prefer it would be the multiplayer screen one rather than the one added here (the mock usage in this one is a touch weird - I'm not too comfortable with half-mocks on concrete classes, always prefer interface mocks if possible).

issue_context.title: Typing after entering wrong password via keyboard in multi starts searching for a room instead
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug:** This does not happen when manually pressing on the join button

**Screenshots or videos showing encountered issue:** 

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53081750/133756197-33ab96b1-2891-40af-96bd-4d6acc47f168.mp4

**osu!lazer version:** 2021.916.0-lazer
comments:
I understand that it's a very unlikely scenario, but this can still happen when doing it very fast, just poiting this out

https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/53081750/134967803-0fad825f-5390-403e-b47a-36bb84fb7736.mp4

review_comments: not sure how to feel about doing this only for the mock in the test - it's a bit of a hidden usage... easy to imagine someone removing at some point thinking it does nothing, only to have the test fall over at runtime
Yeah definitely. Not sure about this one. But at least the test will fail. Will wait for a second opinion.
I dunno, at least it's a leaf object...
Optimally it would be skipped for initial layout, but alas, not simple to do.

I'm not overly familiar with the focus system, so I don't really follow why `TriggerFocusContention()` is used here rather than plain `ChangeFocus()` - if I understand correctly this one doesn't guarantee that the password receives focus? What's the difference?

I'm not too sure. We likely need documentation for these.

I believe that `TriggerFocusContention()` handles scenarios where focus cannot be given to the suggested target better (falling back to the next requesting focus drawable).
